questions.stem: A 60-year-old male, presents with severe chest pain. Coronary angiography shows severe narrowing of circumflex branch of Left coronary artery near its origin. What is the most likely affected part?
A 40-year-old woman was evaluated for her pulmonary stenosis what location is the best auscultation for her valve?

choices.C: The left 2nd intercostal space near the lateral border of sternal body
choices.D: The right 2nd intercostal space near the lateral border of sternal body

questions.stem: A 40-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a car crash. He sustained a blunt injury to the sternum. Which of the following cardiac structures is most likely to be injured?
During surgery on a newborn, a surgeon accidentally damages a structure located near the ductus arteriosus while attempting to ligate it. Which of the following structures is most likely injured?

A 45-year-old man presented with acute abdominal pain. Thoracic magnetic resonance imaging showed anterior disc herniation at the T8-T9 level. Which of the following nerves or trunks is most likely to be compressed?

During a heart transplant procedure, the surgeon inserted his finger through the transverse pericardial sinus. He then pushed backward on the large vessel lying dorsal to his finger. Which of the following vessels is this?
An 8-year-old boy is found to have a midline tumor of the thymus gland. The mass exerts pressure on a posterior blood vessel. Which of the following vessels is most likely to be affected?
In the mid-thoracic region, the esophagus is compressed from the anterior side. Which of the following structures is most likely responsible for this compression?

During coronary bypass surgery, a surgeon prepared the anterior interventricular artery (left anterior descending artery) to receive a graft. He accidentally ligated the adjacent vein. Which of the following veins did he most likely ligate?

During a thoracic surgery near the superior vena cava (SVC), the surgeon observes a large vein crossing anteriorly from the left to the right side to drain into the SVC. Which of the following vessels is most likely being observed?

A histological section from a vessel obtained during abdominal surgery shows the following microscopic features: The tunica intima is thin and lined by a simple endothelium. The tunica media contains only a small number of smooth muscle cells, arranged mainly in a longitudinal direction, and is not well developed. The tunica adventitia, however, is relatively thick and composed of collagen and elastic fibers, with vasa vasorum present within it. Based on these histologic characteristics, which of the following vessels is most likely being described?

A pathologist examines a small blood vessel under the microscope. The tunica intima is thin. The tunica media consists of only 1-5 layers of circularly arranged smooth muscle cells, and there is no distinct internal or external elastic lamina. The tunica adventitia is very thin and poorly developed. Functionally, this vessel is primarily responsible for regulating blood flow into the capillary networks and controlling peripheral vascular resistance. Based on its histological features and function, which type of vessel is this?
A 3-month-old girl has a chest X-ray showed the heart in the right hemithorax, the apex is pointed to the right: which of the heart formation is underdeveloped?

choices.D: Ventral bending of the heart tube
choices.E: Atrial trunk moves ventral to atrium

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man presents with fatigue and dyspnea. An ultrasound examination reveals an atrial septal defect located at the opening of the superior vena cava. Which of the following embryonic structures is most likely underdeveloped?

A newborn presents with cyanosis and echocardiography shows a single large arterial trunk arising from the heart that gives rise to both aorta and pulmonary arteries. Which embryologic defect best explains this condition?
A patient with chronic stable angina is prescribed ivabradine. What is the primary pharmacological action of this drug?
If a subject had the common carotid arteries partially compressed, which of the following would immediately occur?

choices.E: Increased carotid sinus afferent nerve activity

questions.stem: During the plateau phase (Phase 2) of the ventricular action potential, which of the following ion channels is primarily responsible for sustaining depolarization and initiating excitation-contraction coupling?
In a pacemaker cell of the SA node, overdrive suppression occurs when the cell is driven faster than its intrinsic rate. Which of the following mechanisms primarily explains this phenomenon?

choices.A: Increased slope of Phase 4 depolarization due to enhanced funny current (If)
choices.B: Hyperpolarization after rapid pacing due to increased 𝑁𝑎+/𝐾+ATPase activity
choices.C: Prolonged Phase 2 plateau causing delayed repolarization
choices.D: Early activation of L-type 𝐶𝑎2+channels during Phase 3 repolarization
choices.E: Enhanced Phase 0 depolarization mediated by voltage-gated 𝑁𝑎+channels

questions.stem: On an arterial pressure waveform, a small notch appears shortly after the systolic peak. This dicrotic notch is caused by which of the following?

choices.A: Reflex pressure spike from sudden closure of the atrioventricular valves, producing retrograde blood flow into the atria
choices.B: Brief backward flow of arterial blood against the closed semilunar valve due to inertia after ventricular ejection
choices.C: Rapid early diastolic filling of the ventricles causing a transient drop in arterial pressure
choices.D: Active atrial contraction transmitting pressure waves into the arterial system
choices.E: Sudden opening of the semilunar valves at the onset of systole, producing a transient pressure fluctuation

questions.stem: During isovolumetric contraction of the left ventricle, which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: Ventricular volume is at end-diastolic volume (EDV) and pressure rises rapidly
choices.B: Ventricular volume decreases as blood is ejected into the aorta
choices.C: Semilunar valves are open while AV valves remain closed
choices.D: Ventricular pressure falls below atrial pressure and AV valves open
choices.E: Ventricular volume is at end-systolic volume (ESV) and pressure is low

questions.stem: Which of the following events is primarily responsible for the second heart sound (S2)?

choices.A: Aortic pressure greater than ventricular pressure causing closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves
choices.B: Mitral valve opening due to atrial contraction
choices.C: Ventricular contraction generating the first heart sound (S1)
choices.D: Blood flow through the coronary arteries during diastole
choices.E: Closure of the AV valves due to ventricular relaxation

questions.stem: Which of the following events primarily produces the v-wave in the right atrial pressure waveform?

choices.B: Bulging of the tricuspid valve during ventricular contraction
choices.C: Passive filling of the right atrium from systemic veins against a closed tricuspid valve
choices.D: Downward displacement of the tricuspid valve during ventricular systole
choices.E: Closure of the aortic and pulmonary valves

questions.stem: Which of the following factors increases the likelihood of blood flow changing from laminar to turbulent?
The third heart sound (S3) is primarily associated with which physiological event?

choices.A: Closure of the tricuspid and mitral valves
choices.C: Rapid passive filling of the ventricles from the atria
choices.D: Ventricular ejection into the aorta and pulmonary artery
choices.E: Turbulent flow from stenotic semilunar valves

questions.stem: During late diastole, atrial contraction actively contributes to ventricular filling. Which of the following best describes its primary physiological effect?

choices.A: Initiates isovolumetric contraction by abruptly increasing ventricular pressure above atrial pressure
choices.B: Enhances rapid ventricular ejection by increasing systolic pressure
choices.C: Supplies the final 20-30% of ventricular volume prior to systole, increasing end- diastolic volume and stroke volume
choices.D: Generates the S2 heart sound by closure of semilunar valves
choices.E: Facilitates closure of AV valves by creating a pressure gradient across the valves

questions.stem: When afterload increases, what happens to the PV loop?
The S4 heart sound is best explained by what?

choices.A: Turbulent flow through a stenotic valve
choices.B: Closure of the mitral and tricuspid valves
choices.C: Atrial contraction into a stiff ventricle
choices.D: Rapid ventricular filling in early diastole
choices.E: Vibration of papillary muscles during systole

questions.stem: Which of the following is the primary immediate response to an acute drop in systemic arterial pressure?

choices.D: Increased sympathetic activity -> increase HR, contractility, and TPR

questions.stem: Which type of capillaries is typically found in the small intestine and renal glomeruli?
Which of the following is the primary mechanism by which the heart is protected from the high pressure generated during systole?

choices.A: High compliance of the coronary sinus
choices.C: Aortic valve closes, causing a pressure drop during diastole
choices.D: Elastic recoil of the coronary arteries dampening pulse pressure
choices.E: Compression of coronary vessels during contraction

questions.stem: What is the primary mechanism responsible for maintaining a consistent cerebral blood flow across mean arterial pressure ranges from 60 to 169 mmHg?

choices.C: High sensitivity of cerebral arterioles causing release of adenosine
choices.D: High oncotic pressure in cerebral capillaries
choices.E: Pressure gradient between systemic arteries and jugular veins

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man is undergoing assessment of renal blood flow. Various mechanisms act to regulate the resistance of the afferent and efferent arterioles to maintain glomerular filtration rate (GFR). Which of the following correctly matches the mechanism with its primary effect on arteriolar resistance?

choices.C: Increased oncotic pressure in peritubular capillaries

questions.stem: Which vessel in the pulmonary circulation primarily regulates pulmonary vascular resistance in response to local alveolar hypoxia?

What is the primary physiological mechanism by which parasympathetic nervous system stimulation (via acetylcholine) can rapidly produce a negative chronotropic effect (decreased heart rate) in SA node cells?

choices.A: Decreased funny current activity, slowing Phase 4 depolarization
choices.B: Blockade of L-type 𝐶𝑎2+channels during Phase 0
choices.C: Increased 𝐾+efflux (outflow) through ACh-activated 𝐾+channels (IK, ACh)
choices.D: Prolongation of the action potential plateau (Phase 2)

questions.stem: During a transient increase in systemic arterial pressure, which mechanism primarily maintains constant organ perfusion?

choices.C: Afferent arteriole constriction via myogenic response (autoregulation)

questions.stem: When a healthy adult stands up suddenly, venous pooling in the lower body reduces stroke volume. Which systemic response primarily maintains mean arterial pressure?

choices.A: Local nitric oxide-mediated vasodilation in skeletal muscles
choices.B: Rapid renal sodium and water retention
choices.C: Sympathetic-mediated arteriolar constriction increasing total peripheral resistance

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones is primarily responsible for long-term sodium reabsorption in the kidney?

During moderate dynamic exercise, sympathetic activation and local metabolic factors redistribute blood flow. Which of the following vascular beds receives the largest increase in blood flow?

choices.B: Proprioceptors in skeletal muscles and joints

questions.stem: During high-intensity exercise, a subject’s oxygen consumption and CO₂ production rise sharply. Which of the following represents the primary compensatory response to maintain arterial blood gases?

choices.E: Activation of baroreceptors to reduce cardiac output

questions.stem: During a sudden drop in arterial blood pressure, which mechanism is primarily responsible for the rapid increase in systemic vascular resistance?

choices.D: Increased due to local metabolic vasodilation

questions.stem: In a left ventricular PV loop, an increase in pressure (taller loop) with smaller end- systolic volume is most likely caused by what?
In a healthy individual, which primary compensatory adjustment occurs in systemic circulation in response to an increase in blood volume?

choices.A: Decreased heart rate due to baroreceptor reflex
choices.C: Increased total peripheral resistance (TPR) to maintain arterial pressure

questions.stem: During acute moderate blood loss, which of the following is the primary immediate cardiovascular response to maintain arterial blood pressure?

choices.C: Increased total peripheral resistance (TPR) via sympathetic vasoconstriction

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man presents to the emergency department with acute chest pain, fatigue, and sweating for 6 hours. Blood tests are sent for total CK and CK-MB mass. A 58-year-old man presents with chest pain for 3 hours. Which of the following biomarkers is most specific and sensitive for myocardial infarction?

A 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus presents to the emergency department with sudden-onset crushing chest pain radiating to the left arm, associated with sweating and nausea. questions.stem: A term newborn presents with severe cyanosis, tachypnea, single S2, and no definable murmur. Which of the following best explains the mechanism of cyanosis in this patient?

questions.stem: A pediatrician performs the knee-chest maneuver on a child having a hypoxic spell. Which of the following is the main cardiovascular response during this maneuver?
